test_du::diagnostics::test_snippet_points_at_the_unknown_unit_of_block_size, test_du::diagnostics::test_snippet_points_inside_an_attached_block_size, test_du::diagnostics::test_snippet_skips_the_sign_of_a_threshold_with_an_unknown_unit, test_du::diagnostics::test_snippet_underlines_a_zero_block_size and test_du::diagnostics::test_snippet_underlines_the_sign_of_a_rejected_threshold require option-value spans from cli.applet to render source carets; the emitted GNU diagnostics are plain text.

--exclude/--exclude-from are explicitly rejected as unknown options. Remaining uutils failures: test_du::test_du_complex_exclude_patterns, test_du::test_du_exclude, test_du::test_du_exclude_2, test_du::test_du_exclude_from_nonexistent_file, test_du::test_du_exclude_from_read_error, test_du::test_du_exclude_invalid_syntax, test_du::test_du_exclude_mix, test_du::test_du_exclude_several_components and test_du::test_du_time_unaffected_by_exclude. Pattern matching, exclude-file errors and verbose exclusion messages are not implemented.

test_du::test_du_files0_from_missing_file_listed_twice is the remaining --files0-from gap: listed missing operands propagate a runtime fs.stat error with status 3 and stop processing instead of producing one GNU cannot-access diagnostic per name and status 1.

test_du::test_du_h_locale_decimal_separator and test_du::test_du_h_precision differ because human_size uses integer division and a fixed one-decimal approximation; locale decimal separators and GNU's rounding/precision rules are not implemented.

test_du::test_du_inaccessible_directory, test_du::test_du_no_exec_permission, test_du::test_du_no_permission, test_du::test_du_non_existing_files, test_du::test_du_symlink_fail and test_du::test_du_symlink_multiple_fail propagate fs.stat failures as generic runtime errors (status 3) instead of reporting per-path GNU diagnostics and continuing with status 1.

test_du::test_du_dereference_args, test_du::test_du_safe_traversal_with_symlinks and test_du::test_du_symlinks_multiple_links_in_args expose incomplete symlink-directory traversal and argument de-duplication when dereferencing.

test_du::test_du_repeated_time, test_du::test_du_repeated_time_style, test_du::test_du_time, test_du::test_du_time_atime, test_du::test_du_time_directory, test_du::test_du_time_directory_nested, test_du::test_du_time_style_empty and test_du::test_invalid_time_style require --time/--time-style plus timestamps and time-style validation; these options are explicitly rejected.
test_du::test_du_repeated_v expects uutils' repeatable -v option; GNU du has no verbose option, and this applet rejects it rather than accepting an option without behavior.

`test_env::diagnostics::test_snippet_follows_the_string_when_it_is_glued_to_the_option`, `test_snippet_points_at_the_invalid_escape`, `test_snippet_points_at_the_unterminated_quote`, `test_snippet_points_at_the_whole_variable_reference`, and `test_snippet_points_into_the_right_argument` expect uutils source carets for `-S` parse errors. GNU coreutils 9.12 reports plain diagnostics, which XSH follows; a reusable XSH diagnostic mode would need original argv/value spans and a shared terminal caret renderer from `cli.applet`.

`test_env::test_debug_1`, `test_debug_2`, `test_debug1_part_of_string_arg`, and `test_debug2_part_of_string_arg` hard-code a command path ending in `coreutils`; the XSH compatibility stage passes its `xsh-uutests` dispatcher path. XSH prints the executable and argv with the same quoting and indexing as GNU 9.12, so retain the actual staged path.
`test_env::test_env_version` expects `env (uutils coreutils) 0.13.0`; XSH keeps its product version (`env (XSH core) 0.0.1`), and GNU 9.12 identifies itself as GNU coreutils.
`test_env::test_env_french` expects uutils/clap's French `unexpected argument` wording for `--verbo`; GNU 9.12 follows its getopt diagnostic path. Keep GNU option parsing and diagnostics.

`test_env::test_env_overwrite_arg0`, `test_env::test_env_arg_argv0_overwrite`, and `test_env::test_env_arg_argv0_overwrite_mixed_with_string_args` need a child argv[0] override. `process.command_argv` currently drops argv[0] while lowering and `CommandPlan` has no separate argv0 field; add an explicit argv0 field to the shared command plan and carry it through `unix.exec`.

`test_env::test_env_block_signal_flag` and `test_env::test_env_block_realtime_signal` need child signal-mask support, including realtime signal names. The process API exposes signal dispositions but no `sigprocmask` operation or command-plan signal mask; add a typed signal-mask API inherited by `unix.exec` and child plans.

`test_env::test_flags_after_command` and `test_env::test_env_split_quoted_with_backslash_space` use `-i` with a command. `env` explicitly rejects `-i`/`-u` for commands because command plans only inherit the current environment and apply additions; add an inherit/clear mode and unset-name list to `process.command_argv`/`unix.exec` so XSH can construct the requested child environment.

`test_env::test_emoji_env_vars` needs an environment overlay whose name is a non-identifier string (`🎯_VAR`); the XSH environment scope accepts identifier names only. `test_env::test_non_utf8_env_vars` also needs raw environment values: `env.list()` currently requires UTF-8 and errors on `hello\x80world`. Add byte-preserving environment name/value access and allow arbitrary valid byte names/values in child environment overlays.

`test_env::test_ignore_signal_pipe_broken_pipe_regression` sets SIGPIPE to ignore in `env`, then invokes XSH `seq`; the XSH dispatcher resets SIGPIPE to default when the child starts, undoing the disposition that GNU 9.12 preserves through exec. Add a child signal-inheritance policy that lets an exec'd XSH dispatcher retain the caller's ignored dispositions.

test_kill::test_kill_accepts_sigio_alias_for_sending, test_kill::test_kill_with_default_signal, and test_kill::test_kill_with_lower_case_signal_name_old_form cover the SIGIO alias, the default signal selection, and lowercase legacy signal parsing.

test_nohup::test_nohup_help_and_version checks help and version output but its version regex requires `nohup (uutils coreutils) VERSION`; XSH uses the shared `nohup (XSH core) VERSION` convention, while GNU uses `(GNU coreutils)`.

Commands are read a line at a time (RETURN ends each): there is no unbuffered or timed stdin read, so single-key paging, Ctrl-C handling and window-resize redraws are missing (request: an `io.stdin_read`/`unix.read_fd` primitive).
A pipe on standard input is printed in full instead of paged: the commands would have to come from /dev/tty, which has no read primitive.
Non-UTF-8 operands cannot be passed (xsh rejects non-UTF-8 argv): test_more::test_more_non_utf8_paths.

test_more::test_invalid_file_perms needs a non-root user and the lowercase `permission denied` of Rust's ErrorKind; the applet prints strerror text (`Permission denied`) and root can read the file anyway.
-u strips underline and bold overstrikes; there is no terminfo standout mode to switch to otherwise.

GNU `tests/misc/sync.sh` expects `sync FIFO`, `sync -f FIFO`, and `sync -d FIFO` to block until timeout; `fs.fsync` opens FIFO operands in a blocking native filesystem call that the evaluator cannot interrupt to process TERM.

test_timeout::test_invalid_multi_byte_characters and test_timeout::test_invalid_time_interval::case_2_single_quote expect literal characters; under LC_ALL=C GNU quotes invalid interval bytes with C escapes and escapes apostrophes, which the applet follows.
test_timeout::test_zero_timeout places `-s0 -k0` after DURATION. GNU stops option parsing at DURATION and tries to run `-s0` as COMMAND (status 127); the uutils test expects option permutation.
Time zones: TZ is read as UTC or a fixed POSIX offset; an unset TZ reads as UTC instead of /etc/localtime (request: a local-time primitive).
`-p` and `-s` are procps options (not GNU coreutils); they are implemented because the uutils tests exercise them.
test_uptime::test_uptime_with_extra_argument asserts clap wording (`unexpected value 'b'`); the applet prints GNU's `extra operand 'b'`.
test_chgrp::test_chgrp_non_utf8_paths needs raw pathname argv support; the applet receives lossy text before it can call filesystem APIs.
test_chgrp::test_help, test_help_ref, test_ref_help, and test_missing_files assert uutils/clap help and required-argument blocks; the applet uses the shared GNU help and missing-operand diagnostics.
The seven test_chmod::diagnostics cases require uutils source carets and pipe-specific snippets for symbolic-mode errors; cli.applet exposes plain GNU diagnostics without the source spans.
test_chmod::test_chmod_non_utf8_paths and test_chmod::test_gnu_special_filenames need raw pathname argv rather than lossy Str conversion.

Recursive symlink, dangling-target, duplicate-link, preserve-root, and keep-setgid cases expose differences in traversal and lchmod semantics; the two dangling/recursive option combinations, permission-error cases, and too-large modes also need GNU-specific handling.
test_chmod::test_chmod_colored_output and test_gnu_special_options plus test_gnu_usage_matrix cover color, special options, and parser combinations not fully implemented.

test_chown::test_chown_fail_id expects uutils identity lookup and invalid-ID diagnostics; test_chown::test_chown_no_dereference_symlink_to_dir and test_chown::test_chown_symlink_two_links_same_dir expose no-dereference and duplicate-symlink behavior gaps.
test_chown::test_chown_reference_file_with_non_utf8_path needs byte-preserving argv for the --reference pathname.
test_chroot::test_missing_operand expects clap's required-argument block; GNU coreutils 9.12 reports a missing operand with its standard help hint, which XSH follows.
test_groups::test_groups_username and test_groups::test_groups_username_multiple need named-user group lookup; the available auth API only reports the current process groups.

test_id::test_id_single_user, test_id::test_id_multiple_users, test_id::test_id_multiple_users_non_existing, and test_id::test_id_pretty_print_password_record need NSS user/group lookup and complete password records; the current applet resolves only the current identity.
test_install::diagnostics::test_snippet_points_at_the_bad_operator needs the CLI argument span for a source caret.
test_install::test_install_basic_try_reflink needs GNU `--reflink=auto` behavior; test_install::test_install_no_target_directory_failing_usage_with_target_directory expects uutils usage formatting.
test_install::test_install_non_utf8_dir and test_install::test_install_non_utf8_paths need raw pathname argv for the source and destination paths.

test_logname::test_normal and test_logname::test_output_format need a `getlogin()` host API; no typed login-session lookup is available, so XSH reports `no login name` when the host has no login record.
test_logname::test_help expects uutils wording instead of the shared GNU help text.
test_mkfifo::diagnostics::test_snippet_points_at_the_bad_operator expects a source caret; GNU coreutils 9.12 prints `mkfifo: invalid mode`.
test_mknod::diagnostics::test_snippet_points_at_the_bad_operator expects a source caret; GNU coreutils 9.12 prints `mknod: invalid mode`.
test_mknod::test_mknod_invalid_arg expects clap's `unexpected argument` wording; GNU coreutils 9.12 prints `mknod: unrecognized option` and its standard help hint.

test_stat::test_correct_metadata, test_stat::test_multi_files, test_stat::test_normal_format, test_stat::test_symlinks and test_stat::test_terse_normal_format expose signed 64-bit inode/device values where GNU formats the corresponding fields as unsigned; the fs.stat record needs unsigned metadata fields or formatting helpers. test_stat::test_mount_point_width_and_alignment also needs stat's printf flag/width parsing.

test_stat::test_precision_splits_multibyte_char_in_value, test_stat::test_printf, test_stat::test_printf_atime_ctime_mtime_precision, test_stat::test_printf_bel_etc, test_stat::test_printf_octal_1, test_stat::test_printf_octal_2, test_stat::test_printf_octal_out_of_range, test_stat::test_timestamp_format, test_stat::test_timestamp_format_before_epoch, test_stat::test_timestamp_format_before_epoch_truncation and test_stat::test_timestamp_format_preserves_nanoseconds require GNU's printf flags, byte precision, C/octal/hex escapes and precision-aware timestamp directives.

test_stat::diagnostics::test_plain_message_when_stderr_is_a_pipe, test_stat::diagnostics::test_snippet_points_at_the_failing_directive, test_stat::diagnostics::test_snippet_points_inside_a_printf_format, test_stat::test_invalid_directive_after_multibyte_char and test_stat::test_printf_invalid_directive fail because invalid format directives are not validated; test_stat::test_printf_incomplete_hex also needs GNU's incomplete-escape warning. test_stat::test_quoted_name_directive, test_stat::test_quoting_style_env, test_stat::test_quoting_style_invalid_env and test_stat::test_quoting_style_locale require %Qn and the full QUOTING_STYLE behavior, including invalid-value diagnostics and locale-sensitive quoting.

test_stat::test_error_message_preserves_non_utf8_filename and test_stat::test_no_such_directory_message currently receive generic fs.stat runtime errors with status 3 instead of GNU per-file diagnostics with status 1; the first also needs byte-preserving argv in the applet. test_stat::test_without_argument expects uutils/clap's required-argument block, while the applet follows GNU's missing-operand wording.

test_stat::test_stdin_pipe_fifo1, test_stat::test_stdin_pipe_fifo2 and test_stat::test_stdin_redirect require stat '-' to query the metadata of standard input; this needs an fs.fstat-stdin primitive rather than reading stdin bytes.

Integer arguments follow the uutils tests' overflow wording (`Value too large for defined data type`); GNU 9.4 on the host prints `Numerical result out of range`. One constant (`OVERFLOW_TEXT`) in core/stty.xsh flips it if the 9.12 source says otherwise.
Size suffixes of GNU `integer_arg` (`1k`, `2b`) are not accepted; such arguments are `invalid integer argument`.
Fractional speeds (`9600.49`) are accepted as the uutils tests require; GNU 9.4 on the host rejects them as `invalid ispeed`.
Arguments after `--` are settings; GNU 9.4 silently ignores them.

A terminal that keeps other state than requested (a pty drops parity and sizes other than 8 bits) is reported as `unable to perform all requested operations`; GNU 9.4 reports `Invalid argument` for some of those from tcsetattr itself, which `unix.set_tty_attrs` does not raise.
`-g` prints 32 control characters like glibc, but the kernel keeps 19: a saved state that sets later ones is applied and then refused as GNU does.

test_stdbuf::diagnostics::test_plain_message_when_stderr_is_a_pipe and test_stdbuf::test_stdbuf_invalid_mode_fails expect uutils's usage hint for an invalid mode; GNU prints the plain `stdbuf: invalid mode ...` diagnostic without a Try line. test_stdbuf::diagnostics::test_snippet_points_at_the_unknown_unit and test_stdbuf::diagnostics::test_snippet_points_inside_a_long_option_value additionally require option-value spans/carets, which cli.applet does not expose.

test_stdbuf::test_stdbuf_no_buffer_option_fails and test_stdbuf::test_stdbuf_no_command_fails_with_125 assert clap's required-argument block. GNU distinguishes `you must specify a buffering mode option` from `missing operand`; the applet follows GNU and exits 125.
test_stdbuf::test_stdbuf_non_utf8_paths needs byte-preserving argv for command arguments; applet argv is `List[Str]` and cannot represent those path bytes.

test_stdbuf::test_stdbuf_tmpdir_is_private and test_stdbuf::test_tmpdir_with_colon_is_rejected assert uutils's temporary extraction and validation of an embedded libstdbuf. This applet preloads the installed native libstdbuf from system paths, so it creates no TMPDIR library directory and TMPDIR's colon is not part of LD_PRELOAD.
Time zones: TZ is read as UTC or a fixed POSIX offset; an unset TZ reads as UTC instead of /etc/localtime (request: a local-time primitive).

Accounts come from /etc/passwd (`lib.auth`, or XSH_PASSWD_FILE) rather than NSS, and `user.lookup` has no GECOS field (request: `gecos` on `user.lookup`). XSH_UTMP_FILE replaces /var/run/utmp for tests.
`--lookup` canonicalizes nothing: `dns` has no canonical name (getaddrinfo AI_CANONNAME), so numeric hosts pass and a host name fails with an explicit message (request: `dns.canonical`).
Sessions of the default utmp file are checked for live pids (`process.kill` with signal 0) as gnulib does; an explicit FILE is listed as written.

Time zones: TZ is read as UTC or a fixed POSIX offset (`EST5`, `<+03>-3`); zone names and DST rules need a tz database, and an unset TZ reads as UTC instead of /etc/localtime (request: a local-time primitive).

`who -b` and the boot record synthesized for a default utmp file without one derive the boot time from `unix.uptime_seconds` (whole seconds), so it can differ from GNU's by a second at a minute boundary.
`--lookup` canonicalizes nothing: `dns` has no canonical name (getaddrinfo AI_CANONNAME), so numeric hosts pass and a host name fails with an explicit message (request: `dns.canonical`).

`test_who::test_too_many_args` expects clap's `unexpected value` wording; XSH reports GNU's `extra operand` diagnostic. `test_who::test_piped_to_dev_full` and `test_who::test_short_list_piped_to_dev_full` expect `who: No space left on device`; pinned GNU 9.12 and XSH report `who: write error: No space left on device`.
